g2.label: 2 — three applications so far

g6.label: 6 — ___ you ever visited a factory?

g7.label: 7 — When ___ you start?

g8.label: 8 — Anna ___ already finished

g1.label: 1 — you have to write an ___

g2.label: 2 — the document listing school and skills

g4.label: 4 — employees get their ___

g5.label: 5 — her ___ showed her round

g6.label: 6 — always be ___

g7.label: 7 — a vet ___ sick animals

g8.label: 8 — students start an ___
g8.why: An apprenticeship (Ausbildung) combines working in a company with vocational school.

g2.label: 2 — the colour of their ___

g3.label: 3 — he became a ___
g3.why: Mandela studied law, so he became a lawyer.

g4.label: 4 — sent him to ___ for life
g4.why: In 1964 the court sentenced him to life in prison.

g5.label: 5 — break stones in the hot ___

g6.label: 6 — demanded his ___

g7.label: 7 — its first free ___

g8.label: 8 — every group had the same ___

g1.label: 1 — a man ___ never gave up

g2.label: 2 — a system ___ separated people

g3.label: 3 — the place ___ he spent 18 years

g4.label: 4 — the year ___ the election was held
g4.why: "The year" is a time, so use when.

g5.label: 5 — families ___ homes had been destroyed

g6.label: 6 — the party ___ he joined
g6.why: The ANC is a thing (a party), so use which.

g7.label: 7 — Cape Town, ___ lies in the south-west
g7.why: After a comma (non-defining clause) English uses which, never that.

g8.label: 8 — the journalist ___ interviewed Mandela
g8.why: "The journalist" is a person, so use who.

g1.label: 1 — not allowed to ___ in elections
g1.why: Under apartheid, black South Africans were not allowed to vote.

g2.label: 2 — he fought for ___
g2.why: Equality means everybody having the same rights — what Mandela fought for.

g3.label: 3 — a ___ outside a city
g3.why: A township is the poor area outside a city where black families had to live.

g4.label: 4 — finally ___ from prison
g4.why: To be released from prison means to be set free.

g5.label: 5 — eleven official ___
g5.why: South Africa has eleven official languages, among them English, Zulu and Afrikaans.

g6.label: 6 — a peaceful ___
g6.why: A protest is a public action against something people think is wrong.

g7.label: 7 — the Nobel ___ Prize
g7.why: Mandela and de Klerk received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993.

g8.label: 8 — the ___ Nation
g8.why: South Africa is called the Rainbow Nation because of its many different groups.

g1.label: 1 — how they use their ___
g1.why: The study asked teenagers how they use their phones.

g2.label: 2 — social ___
g2.why: "Social media" is the fixed phrase for platforms like Instagram or TikTok.

g3.label: 3 — they chat with ___
g3.why: You chat with people — friends, not fridges or frames.

g4.label: 4 — they sometimes feel ___
g4.why: "Feel stressed" describes the pressure of comparing yourself with perfect pictures.

g5.label: 5 — fake ___
g5.why: "Fake news" is the set phrase for false stories that look real.

g6.label: 6 — check the ___ of a story
g6.why: The source of a story is where it originally comes from.

g7.label: 7 — how to ___ such messages
g7.why: You report a cruel message so that the platform or the school can act on it.

g8.label: 8 — simple ___

g1.label: 1 — she said she ___ tired

g2.label: 2 — they ___ videos every evening

g3.label: 3 — he ___ the photo

g4.label: 4 — she ___ call me later
g4.why: "Will" becomes "would" in reported speech.

g5.label: 5 — he ___ find the link
g5.why: "Can't" becomes "couldn't" in reported speech.

g6.label: 6 — we ___ check the source
g6.why: "Must" becomes "had to" in reported speech.

g7.label: 7 — he ___ a picture
g7.why: The present progressive "am posting" becomes the past progressive "was posting".

g8.label: 8 — her phone ___ the day before
g8.why: The simple past "broke" goes one step back to the past perfect "had broken".

g1.label: 1 — where I ___ my news
g1.why: A reported question keeps normal word order and drops "do/does/did".

g2.label: 2 — he asked ___ I was online
g2.why: A yes/no question is reported with if (or whether).

g3.label: 3 — told us ___ that video
g3.why: A negative order is reported with not to + infinitive.

g4.label: 4 — she asked me ___ off my phone
g4.why: A request is reported with to + infinitive after "asked me".

g5.label: 5 — Mia ___ me that...
g5.why: "Tell" needs a person after it: told me that...

g6.label: 6 — Ben ___ that...
g6.why: "Say" is used without a person: he said that...

g7.label: 7 — how many followers I ___ got
g7.why: After "asked", "have got" shifts back to "had got".

g8.label: 8 — she asked me ___ I had read it
g8.why: A yes/no question ("Did you...?") is reported with whether or if.

g1.why: Doctors recommend eight to ten hours of sleep a night for teenagers.

g2.label: 2 — blue light tells the ___

g3.label: 3 — a quick ___ between lessons

g4.label: 4 — sugar and ___

g5.label: 5 — they can ___ better
g5.why: To concentrate means to keep your attention on something.

g6.label: 6 — thirty minutes of ___
g6.why: Exercise is physical activity; thirty minutes a day is the recommendation.

g7.label: 7 — hormones improve your ___

g8.label: 8 — good for your mental ___

g1.label: 1 — if you ___ more water

g2.label: 2 — she ___ so tired tomorrow

g3.label: 3 — if you ___ your phone off
g3.why: After if you use the present simple, even when you mean the future.

g4.label: 4 — if we ___ to school
g4.why: The if-clause takes the present simple: if we cycle.

g5.label: 5 — he ___ sleep tonight
g5.why: The result of a real possibility is expressed with will / won't.

g6.label: 6 — if it ___ tomorrow
g6.why: After if you need the present simple, third person singular: rains.

g7.label: 7 — if you ___ them in the kitchen
g7.why: The if-clause takes the present simple: if you help them.

g8.label: 8 — if I ___ time after school
g8.why: After if you use the present simple; the will is already in "I'll come".

g1.label: 1 — if I ___ more free time
g1.why: Type II uses the simple past in the if-clause: if I had more time.

g2.label: 2 — she ___ so tired
g2.why: The main clause of a type II sentence takes would / wouldn't + infinitive.

g3.label: 3 — if you ___ a personal trainer
g3.why: "What would you do if...?" needs the simple past in the if-clause.

g4.label: 4 — if we ___ a swimming pool
g4.why: The if-clause of a type II sentence takes the simple past, not would.

g5.label: 5 — if he ___ less television
g5.why: After if you use the simple past: if he watched less television.

g6.label: 6 — if I ___ you
g6.why: In "If I were you" English uses were, not was, for imagined situations.

g7.label: 7 — if everybody ___ the rules
g7.why: The if-clause takes the simple past — never "would" in the if-part.

g8.label: 8 — she ___ much more energy
g8.why: The main clause of a type II sentence takes would + infinitive.

g1.label: 1 — a school-leaving ___
g1.why: A school-leaving certificate is the document you get when you finish Year 10.

g2.label: 2 — a vocational ___
g2.why: In an apprenticeship you spend part of the week at a vocational school.

g4.label: 4 — a careers ___

g5.label: 5 — free ___ from the agency

g6.label: 6 — take a ___ year
g6.why: A gap year is a year off between school and work or study.

g7.label: 7 — for their whole ___
g7.why: "For their whole life" means for as long as they live.

g8.label: 8 — ask ___ early
g8.why: You ask questions — of teachers, parents and people who already do the job.

g1.label: 1 — it ___ rain

g2.label: 2 — I ___ answer it
g2.why: The decision is made at the moment of speaking, so use will.

g3.label: 3 — she ___ to London next Friday

g4.label: 4 — robots ___ do many jobs
g4.why: "I think" plus a prediction about 2050 takes will.

g5.label: 5 — we ___ visit the careers fair
g5.why: They have already registered, so it is an existing plan: going to.

g6.label: 6 — my train ___ at 7.15
g6.why: Timetables take the present simple: the train leaves at 7.15.

g7.label: 7 — ___ you help me?
g7.why: A polite request is made with "Will you...?"

g8.label: 8 — he ___ pass the test
g8.why: This is a prediction based on evidence, so use won't + infinitive.

g1.label: 1 — when I ___ home
g1.why: After when you use the present simple, even for future time.

g2.label: 2 — as soon as she ___ her results
g2.why: After "as soon as" use the present simple, third person singular: receives.

g3.label: 3 — until everybody ___ here
g3.why: After until you use the present tense, not will.

g4.label: 4 — before he ___ his placement
g4.why: After before you use the present simple.

g5.label: 5 — after I finish school, I ___ travel
g5.why: This half is the main clause, so the will belongs here.

g6.label: 6 — if the course ___ too expensive
g6.why: After if you use the present simple; the won't goes in the other half.

g7.label: 7 — when she ___ the room
g7.why: After when you use the present simple: when she enters.

g8.label: 8 — I ___ send you a message
g8.why: This is the main clause, so it takes will; the as-soon-as clause stays present.
